description: Every recorded difference between a GUI.Forms control and the observable contract of its Windows Forms counterpart. GUI.Forms matches Windows Forms' documented observable behaviour, not its internals or timings, and records each difference here (owner rule). Checked by tools/winforms_divergences.py; docs/controls/generated/winforms-divergences.md is rendered from it.

divergences.winforms: When focus leaves the grid and a RowValidating handler cancels, the grid keeps focus and the current cell stays in the row.
divergences.gui_forms: When focus leaves the grid, the edit commits and the current row validates; a cancel skips row_validated, but focus is not held: it moves where the user sent it.
divergences.reason: Focus moves before the grid learns of it (Window::focused_control_changed), and taking it back from the window's focus change would let one control veto another's focus, which no other control may do.

divergences.winforms: BackColor paints the control's background; the check box's square stays white.
divergences.gui_forms: The control's own back_color also fills the check box's square.
divergences.reason: Stage T4's Control colours work: a control's back colour is the fill of its own surfaces, the square included, so one colour themes the whole control.

divergences.winforms: Merge matches a source item to a target item by its Text, compared case-insensitively in the current culture.
divergences.gui_forms: merge_strips compares displayed text with ASCII-only case folding.
divergences.reason: Culture-dependent comparison would make a merge depend on the user's locale; the strip ID and merge_index give exact matching where text is not enough.

divergences.winforms: Merge accepts any two ToolStrips that allow merging, including a ToolStrip into a MenuStrip.
divergences.gui_forms: Only strips of the same kind merge: the ToolStrip family with the ToolStrip family, MenuStrip with MenuStrip.
divergences.reason: A MenuStrip's top level holds menus only (MenuStripItemSpec), a ToolStrip's holds buttons, labels and hosted items; there is no item that is both.

divergences.winforms: Items carry no identity, so any merge result is accepted.
divergences.gui_forms: A merge whose result would repeat an item ID in the target is refused: merge_strips returns false and changes nothing.
divergences.reason: Items are addressed by stable IDs (clicks, check state, semantics); a repeated ID would make them ambiguous.

divergences.winforms: A moved ToolStripControlHost keeps its hosted control and that control's state.
divergences.gui_forms: A moved hosted item (combo box, text box, progress bar) is recreated in the target, so its control's state is not carried.
divergences.reason: A hosted control is owned by its strip; moving it between owners is not part of the strip's item system.

divergences.winforms: MatchOnly merges the drop-down items of a matched ToolStripDropDownItem, creating its drop-down as needed.
divergences.gui_forms: match_only recurses only when the matched item already holds a menu (a drop-down or split button, a menu strip item, a submenu).
divergences.reason: An item's kind fixes whether it holds a menu; a merge does not change a target item's kind.

divergences.winforms: A drop-down left without items by a merge still shows an empty drop-down.
divergences.gui_forms: A menu a merge empties stays valid and is not shown until it has items again.
divergences.reason: An empty menu has nothing to choose; showing it would be a dead end.

divergences.winforms: Dark mode follows Application.SetColorMode (.NET 9 and later): SystemColors are replaced by a dark system palette.
divergences.gui_forms: Dark mode is a theme variant. A theme declares color-scheme: light dark. ApplicationResources::set_automatic_colour_scheme, off by default, follows the host's preference. A theme with no dark variant is shown as GUI.Forms' own dark theme, with warning W403.
divergences.reason: Themes are the single home of colour; the fallback gives every application a working dark mode without per-control colours (owner 2026-11-04).

divergences.winforms: A control's default colours are SystemColors (Control, ControlText, Window, Highlight), read from the system.
divergences.gui_forms: A control's default colours come from the application's theme. The system's accent and highlight colours are only hints, which a theme can read with env(system-accent, ...) and env(system-highlight, ...) or ignore.
divergences.reason: Colour belongs to the theme, so that one theme looks the same on every host (T4 theme variants).

divergences.winforms: Under a Windows contrast theme, controls paint with SystemColors, which take the contrast theme's palette.
divergences.gui_forms: Windows' contrast palette is not taken. GUI.Forms switches to its own high-contrast mode, with its own palette, swapped in at paint time.
divergences.reason: The owner judged the host contrast palettes unreliable; GUI.Forms' own palette meets its 7:1 contrast gate in every state (T4 D2).

divergences.winforms: BackColor and ForeColor apply in every presentation and are ordinary practice.
divergences.gui_forms: They apply under the application's theme, and the first time each is set on a control it writes the warning W404 inline_colour. While a window shows GUI.Forms' own theme as a fallback for a missing dark or light variant, they are suspended.
divergences.reason: A colour set on a control cannot adapt to a theme's light and dark variants, and painting a light-mode colour over the dark fallback breaks the look. Colour belongs in theme rules (T4 theme variants, stage A).

divergences.winforms: SetColumnSpan and SetRowSpan apply to any child; a child without an explicit cell is auto-placed into the first free run of cells its span needs.
divergences.gui_forms: A span needs an explicit cell: writing a span other than 1 to an automatically placed child is refused, and automatic placement gives each child one cell.
divergences.reason: The table holds the spans as anonymous GridSpan objects anchored at a child's cell (study 10.9 section 5); an automatic child has no anchor. Coordinator for cp20: automatic placement ignores spans.

divergences.winforms: Spans may overlap other spans or explicitly placed children; the layout then moves the later child on (or leaves it out under FixedSize).
divergences.gui_forms: A span that would overlap another span or cover another child's cell, and a cell inside another child's span, are refused with std::invalid_argument when written.
divergences.reason: The table's spans follow the GridSpan conflict rules (study 10.9 section 1, rules a and d), so a fused region never holds a second placed child.

divergences.winforms: Dragging draws a split line and resizes the target on release; Escape during the drag cancels and the target keeps its size. The splitter has no keyboard input.
divergences.gui_forms: Dragging resizes the target live (splitter_moving before each step). Escape, losing the pointer capture and the window's deactivation cancel and put the target back at its size before the drag. The begin_keyboard_drag rule action moves the bar from the keyboard (arrows by 10, Ctrl 100, Shift 1; Enter keeps, Escape restores).
divergences.reason: The drag runs on the drag engine, whose cancels never leave a model changed; the observable end of Escape is Windows Forms'. Live resizing was already GUI.Forms' behaviour, and the keyboard path is the engine's accessibility rule (every drag has a keyboard equivalent).

divergences.winforms: Escape during a splitter drag cancels it and the distance stays where it was before the drag; losing the capture ends the drag. The focused splitter moves by SplitterIncrement with the arrow keys.
divergences.gui_forms: Escape, losing the pointer capture and the window's deactivation cancel the drag and put back the distance from before it (SplitChangeReason::cancel). Besides the focused arrows, the begin_keyboard_drag rule action on splitter_control runs a keyboard drag (arrows by keyboard_increment, Ctrl ten steps, Shift a tenth; Enter keeps, Escape restores).
divergences.reason: The seam drag runs on the drag engine, as the Splitter's does, and the engine's cancels never leave a model changed (before the engine a lost capture kept the dragged distance). The keyboard drag is the engine's accessibility rule.
